title: Annotatio II §.VI: Calixtus — our men once approved Absolute Decree, then retreated to first-four-centuries foreknowledge sentence; Hunnius labored much
pass_a_gloss: Our men (says the often-praised Calixtus), from among whom formerly many likewise approved the Absolute Decree, gradually withdrew themselves to the Sentence of the first Four Centuries (namely, a Decree made according to foreknowledge), in which matter Aegidius Hunnius labored much and outstandingly:
pass_b_english: As the often-praised Calixtus puts it: many of our own once approved the Absolute Decree as well, then by degrees fell back to the teaching of the first four centuries — a decree framed according to foreknowledge — and Aegidius Hunnius did a great and distinguished work in that change:
source_text: Nostri (inquit saepius laudatus Calixtus) è quibus olim multi itidem Absolutum Decretum approbarunt, paulatim ad Sententiam primorum Quatuor Seculorum (nempe Decretum juxta praescientiam factum) sese receperunt, qua in re multùm & egregiè laboravit Ægidius Hunnius:

lemmas.gloss: sentence of the first Four Centuries

lemmas.note: Hunnius as chief worker of the turn

rejected: praescientia as mere awareness without decree

notes: Hexades Annotatio II §.VI densify §192; Calixtus citation on Absolute Decree to foreknowledge turn.
